main.title: Stanford CS234: Reinforcement Learning
main.why: MDPs, TD and Q-learning up to DQN, policy gradients up to PPO, imitation, RLHF and DPO, offline RL, bandits and tree search. In English.

further.title: UC Berkeley CS 285: Deep Reinforcement Learning

main.title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences
main.why: Waiting for final outcomes makes learning slow, so temporal-difference methods learn from the difference between successive predictions.

main.title: Q-learning
main.why: Q-learning learns optimal action values while following any exploring policy, converging as long as every action keeps being tried.

main.title: Human-Level Control through Deep Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Q-learning with neural networks was unstable, so DQN adds experience replay and a target network to learn Atari games from pixels.

further.title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning

main.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Without a model of the environment, REINFORCE follows the gradient of expected reward estimated from sampled actions and rewards.

main.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization
main.why: Large policy-gradient steps can collapse a policy, so TRPO keeps each update inside a KL-divergence trust region.

main.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
main.why: TRPO is complex to implement, so PPO clips its objective to get similarly safe steps from plain minibatch updates.

further.title: Implementation Matters in Deep Policy Gradients: A Case Study on PPO and TRPO

main.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
main.why: Deep RL for continuous control was sample-hungry and brittle, so SAC learns off-policy while maximizing reward plus entropy.

main.title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search
main.why: Go is too large for brute-force search, so AlphaGo guides tree search with policy and value networks trained on human games and self-play.

main.title: Mastering the Game of Go without Human Knowledge
main.why: AlphaGo Zero drops human games and learns from self-play alone, with tree search as the teacher for its network.

main.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
main.why: Planning usually needs the game's rules, so MuZero plans with a learned model that predicts only reward, policy and value.

main.title: Mastering Diverse Control Tasks through World Models
main.why: RL algorithms usually need retuning for each domain, so DreamerV3 learns a world model and trains in imagined rollouts with one fixed configuration.

main.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
main.why: A cloned policy drifts into states the expert never showed, so DAgger has the expert label the states the learner visits.

main.title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning
main.why: Offline RL overestimates actions missing from the data, so CQL pushes their Q-values down while training on a fixed dataset.

background.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems

main.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
main.why: Many tasks lack a reward function, so a reward model fit to human comparisons of short clips trains the agent instead.

further.title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback

main.title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation
main.why: New articles need exploration, so LinUCB picks Yahoo front-page news by upper confidence bounds over user and article features.

background.title: Finite-Time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

further.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Thompson Sampling

main.why: Heuristics decided which map area to search, so Airbnb frames it as a contextual bandit that explores with UCB on dropout-based uncertainty.

main.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
main.why: Point estimates from a few runs per task mislead, so report bootstrap intervals, performance profiles and interquartile means.

main.title: Top-K Off-Policy Correction for a REINFORCE Recommender System
main.why: Logs from older recommenders bias policy learning, so YouTube trains a REINFORCE recommender with off-policy correction.

main.title: A Better Match for Drivers and Riders: Reinforcement Learning at Lyft
main.why: To find more efficient matches, Lyft estimates each driver's future earnings in real time with online RL and matches on them.
